newsitem.title: UK: PAL eyes ex-UK spring cargo rate rise.
newsitem.headline: PAL eyes ex-UK spring cargo rate rise.

text.p: Philippines Airlines (PAL) is studying a possible spring ex-UK air cargo rates increase but there are no immediate plans for any rise, UK cargo manager Keith O'Callaghan told Reuters.
"It will be the status quo until at least April 1, as we are still evaluating the situation. But even then, any increase could be delayed until May 1," he said in a telephone interview.
PAL did not apply the six pence a kg air cargo fuel surcharge adopted by many airlines operating out of the UK in November 1996, he added.
Earlier this week British Airways Plc World Cargo division said that it was increasing ex-UK rates to Asian destinations by seven percent from March 17.
O'Callaghan also said that PAL will introduce an extra non-stop flight between Manila and London-Heathrow from March 30 using long range Airbus Industrie A340-200 passenger aircraft.
This will provide four flights a week, rising to five in June and hopefully six a week by end-1997, he said.
